chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim ibn Uthman from Hammad from Hariz from Abu Usamah who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom, indeed these collectors come to us and take the charity (sadaqah/zakat) from us, so we give it to them; does it count for us?' He said, 'No, indeed these are a people who have taken it from you by force,' or he said, 'They have wronged you regarding your wealth,' and indeed the charity is only for its rightful recipients.

This report indicates what we mentioned, that it is preferable to return it (pay again). It is also possible that what is meant by his saying 'No, it does not count' is that it does not count for the other wealth, because when they take the zakat of the crops/produce, they take more than what is due, so it is not permissible for him to count the excess from the zakat of gold and silver and other things. Rather, it must be paid out separately. And it was permitted and allowed that one does not pay out a second time from the very thing from which it was taken. As for that which indicates that the charity of the produce is not due more than once, is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Does paying zakat to collectors who take more than the required amount fulfill the religious obligation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi cites this hadith to establish the principle that if collectors seize more than the obligatory zakat amount, the payer's obligation is not fully discharged due to the element of compulsion (ghasb). While it is permissible to count the excess within the original payment, it is preferable to pay the zakat again separately to ensure the obligation is fulfilled correctly, reflecting the scholarly view that the excess was taken wrongfully rather than as a voluntary discharge.
